title: Grade 4 Science — How Traits Help Living Things Survive
subject: Science
description: Practice with questions on camouflage, behaviors, structures, environment.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: A snowshoe hare's broad feet help it do what?
What helps a cactus lose less water in a dry place?
A walking stick insect looks like a twig. How may that help it?
choices: It becomes heavier than a twig.

questions.question: Why are many duck feet webbed?
choices: They push water better while swimming.

questions.question: Which bird beak is useful for cracking hard seeds?
choices: a long, thin beak for nectar

questions.question: What helps many fish move through water with less drag?
Why do some birds migrate before winter?
choices: They never need water while flying.
They can reach places with more food.

questions.question: How can thick fur help a mammal in a cold habitat?
choices: It stops the animal from eating.
It makes the air warm everywhere.

questions.question: How do lungs help a whale even though it lives in water?
choices: They allow it to stay underwater forever.
They help its skin make food from sunlight.
They take in oxygen from air when it surfaces.
They take oxygen directly from water like gills.

questions.question: Why are many seeds with hooks carried to new places?
choices: They are pulled only by magnets.

questions.question: Some flowers bloom at night. Which visitor might move pollen between them?
choices: an insect that only visits in daylight

questions.question: How can warning colors protect some animals?
choices: Bright colors make all sounds quiet.
Colors stop an animal from needing food.
All warning colors blend into snow.

questions.question: What behavior can help a desert animal avoid daytime heat?
choices: stay in direct sun at noon
climb into a sun-heated rock crack at noon
rest in a burrow by day
leave its shelter at the hottest hour

questions.question: Why might a plant with deep roots fare well during a short drought?
choices: Its roots can reach moisture farther down.

questions.question: How can a flat body and a mottled pattern help a bottom-dwelling fish?
choices: They help it blend with the bottom.
They allow it to breathe air forever.
They help it climb trees for food.
They change salt water to fresh.

questions.question: Which action is a behavior rather than a body structure?
choices: seeking shade on a hot day

questions.question: What can sharp, hooked talons help a hawk do?
Why can broad leaves help some plants grow in shade?
choices: They make the soil hotter at night.
They collect more of the available light.
They stop other plants from growing.

questions.question: How might a hollow tree help a bat survive winter?
choices: It produces fish for the bat.
It stops the air from cooling.
It can provide shelter from cold wind.

questions.question: In a rocky place, brown beetles are harder for birds to see than bright white ones. Which advantage could they have?
choices: They may be eaten less often.
They change the color of the rocks.
